decisions.quote:
This project investigates the reliability and reproducibility of a paper accepted for publication in a top machine learning
                                         conference. The models have been implemented using code and information provided by the authors.
decisions.reason: The study re-implements and runs the original authors' provided code and inspects their pre-trained models on one of the original study's own datasets (FFHQ, alongside an additional smaller Cartoon dataset due to compute limits) to verify the computational experiments of Hudson and Zitnick (2021). Under the codebook, re-analysing the original study's code and data is a reproduction.

decisions.location: Independent raw primary passage G-compute-setting; complete original-specific source context and preflight0159
decisions.quote:
Considering that we had only one GPU and not enough time to reproduce this setting, we decided to resize the images
from 256 × 256 to 64 × 64 resolution for the Google Carton Set and to 128 × 128 for the FFHQ dataset.
For the GANformer, we select k = 32 latent variables.
All models have been trained for the same number of steps, 300 000 image training samples (300 kimg), while the
paper presents results after training 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000 and 10000 kimg samples.
decisions.reason: Preserve the established reproduction type for the central original-code/FFHQ verification, with the separate Cartoon extension explicitly distinguished. The authors substantially resize images, shorten training, merge/simplify code and alter architecture; their implementation-success statement does not establish original numerical recovery. Paper/code hyperparameter and released-checkpoint architecture discrepancies are directly inspected, but neither these discrepancies nor poorer output under modified settings establish failure of an identical original numerical computation. That recovery axis is genuinely undetermined here. On robustness, the adapted original FFHQ analyses directly compare duplex variants against the baseline and conclude that declared quality/efficiency improvements were not achieved. This is a bounded substantive challenge under changed training/architecture, not an inference from the unrelated Cartoon-only result or a full-scale original-code failure. Preserve the final expert axes/rationale as a contrary opinion, without adopting the unsupported recovery inference.

previous_decisions.quote: In this study, we have first implemented a Google Colab Pro compatible version of the authors’ code, enabling us to train and test StyleGAN2 and the two flavours of GANformer (Duplex and Simplex attention) in less than 54 hours in total. As presented in Section 5, we could not achieve the improvements declared by the authors but instead found a decrease in time performance and quality using duplex attention.
previous_decisions.location: Section 8 Discussion and conclusion, p. 9, lines 477-480
previous_decisions.reason: Re-running the authors' code on the original FFHQ dataset (under reduced resolution and training steps) and comparing against the original paper's reported metrics produced numerical output that failed to recover the claimed FID and efficiency improvements over StyleGAN2 and revealed discrepancies between the published methodology/hyperparameters and the released code/pre-trained models (computational issues). Testing alternative training and architectural specifications on FFHQ (including removing discriminator attention to match the pre-trained models) still failed to support the superiority of duplex attention over StyleGAN2 (robustness challenges).
